meaning: The rounded number of men mustered in the camp of Dan
description: The number 157,000 appears as part of 157,600, which is the total count of fighting men mustered in Dan's camp during the wilderness journey (Num 2:31). Dan's camp included the tribes of Dan, Asher, and Naphtali, and was the largest of the four camp groups surrounding the tabernacle. This camp was assigned the position north of the tabernacle and held the last place in the marching order – they were to "break camp last, under their banners". The fact that Dan's camp was the most numerous, yet still placed last, emphasizes that the camp arrangement did not follow mere numerical strength, but a divine ordinance for Israel's organization in the wilderness.

footnotes.text: The camp of Dan consisted of Dan (62,700), Asher (41,500) and Naphtali (53,400), totaling 157,600 fighting men according to Numbers 1–2.

In rabbinic tradition, Dan's placement at the rear of the marching order has been linked to the tribe's role as a kind of "rear guard" that gathered stragglers, cf. Deuteronomy 25:18 where Amalek attacked precisely the rear guard.
